subject.title: fix(tts): defer text settlement for final-mode TTS to eliminate churn (#83511)

question: Should OpenClaw expose `captionedFinalText` as a stable channel-plugin capability, or should the TTS churn repair be narrowed to a Telegram-owned implementation until a broader contract is approved?
rationale: The branch changes a plugin SDK capability whose opt-in semantics control visible message suppression across present and future channel plugins; code review cannot determine the intended permanent API boundary.

options.title: Approve the capability contract
options.body: Treat `captionedFinalText` as a supported channel-plugin API after current-head Telegram proof confirms the documented delivery and fallback behavior.

options.title: Narrow to Telegram
options.body: Keep the user-facing repair but move caption-specific policy into the Telegram owner boundary and defer a reusable SDK capability proposal.

options.title: Pause the direction
options.body: Leave the existing behavior unchanged until maintainers define the intended cross-channel final-TTS delivery contract.

recommendation.title: Approve the capability contract
recommendation.body: Treat `captionedFinalText` as a supported channel-plugin API after current-head Telegram proof confirms the documented delivery and fallback behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Feature-history evidence most strongly connects steipete to the shared ACP, reply-dispatch, and channel-capability boundaries implicated by the API decision.
